subject: Customer request: compatibility exemption + migration timeline for text-infer-v1
messages:
From: Samir Shah <samir@nebulaanalytics.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@nebulaanalytics.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Request: compatibility exemption + migration window for text-infer-v1

Marcus —

Quick context: Nebula runs a set of high-throughput inference pipelines that depend on several undocumented quirks of text-infer-v1 (tokenizer edge behavior + a lightweight pre-token filter). We saw the deprecation notice last week and need a short-term plan because our workloads are in production and tied to a quarter-end reporting pipeline.

Asks:
- Request an explicit compatibility exemption (read-only passthrough) for 30 days beyond your published deprecation window so we can complete validation without service interruptions.
- A clear migration timeline and a contact (POC) on the Redwood side for technical questions during the migration.

We can provide a small test corpus and the list of model behaviours we rely on. Happy to sign an addendum if needed.

Thanks,
Samir Shah
VP Engineering, Nebula Analytics
Attachment: compat-matrix.csv (summary of tokenization cases)
From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: compatibility exemption + migration window for text-infer-v1

Folks — forwarding a customer ask that needs cross-functional confirmation. Key items below.

Summary of customer asks (from Samir):
- 30-day compatibility exemption (passthrough behavior) after deprecation date
- A named POC for technical migration help

Product questions / decisions needed:
1) Can we support a 30-day passthrough mode for text-infer-v1 for a single account without impacting our rollback and SLOs? (Specifically: will kv-cache and prefix-caching be left intact?)
2) What is the minimum engineering effort to provide a compatibility flag in the hosted API vs. requiring them to run a private deployment?
3) Docs/comm cadence: what do we tell other customers — isolated exemption vs. public extension?

Operational asks (engineering/capacity):
- Karthik: can you confirm if Dedicated pools have capacity to host a single-account passthrough or if we need to route them to a compatibility-only variant?
- Monica (CS): agree to be the POC and run validation with Nebula — can you confirm support SLAs and how much engineering time we should reserve?

Proposed next steps:
- Quick triage call today (30 min) to align the minimum-safe option and calendar the canary window.
- If agreed, deliver a short exemption agreement and an internal runbook (I attached a starter migration-checklist.xlsx).

If you need, I can take point on the customer comms and legal coordination.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference
Attachment: migration-checklist.xlsx
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 11:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: compatibility exemption + migration window for text-infer-v1

Thanks for flagging Marcus. Short answers and constraints from Product: 

- 30-day passthrough: acceptable as a customer-specific, timeboxed exception if we gate it behind an agreement that limits scope (no SLA extension, support hours capped, audit log enabled). We should not change the public deprecation date.
- API approach: preferred path is a compatibility flag on the hosted API for accounts we whitelist — lower friction than forcing private deploys. Engineering needs to confirm safety.
- Comms: we should treat this as a one-off and publish a short note in the migration KB documenting the exemption for transparency.

Requirements for the exemption to be approved by Product: 
1) Engineering sign-off on no-regression testing matrix within 5 business days.
2) CS POC (Monica) to collect validation artifacts and confirm the test corpus.
3) Legal to sign the short-term addendum before we enable passthrough.

I can coordinate the customer-facing timeline and draft the KB note. Proposed milestone dates (tentative):
- Engineering sign-off: 2027-03-25
- Legal addendum signed: 2027-03-26
- Enable passthrough / start canary: 2027-03-28 (30 days)

I'll add a two-line public note in the migration playbook mentioning Nebula's exemption window (no SLA changes).

-Laura Bennett
Senior PM, Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: compatibility exemption + migration window for text-infer-v1

+1 on the plan. Quick engineering notes and capacity checks: 

- Dedicated pools: we can spin up an isolated compatibility pool for Nebula for the 30-day window; latency impact should be negligible if we reserve one node (will need cost approval).
- Hosted compatibility flag: the runtime change is minimal — a request-path passthrough mode that bypasses the tokenizer shim for flagged accounts. Risk: small surface area around KV cache keying and metric attribution. We'll run the no-regression tests Laura asked for, estimated 48–72 hours to complete.
- Canary schedule: propose canary start 2027-03-28, full enable for Nebula 2027-03-29 if tests pass. I'll post the canary calendar invite (canary-calendar.ics attached) and a short internal rollback playbook.

Operational asks for CS/Legal/Product: 
- Monica: please confirm test corpus delivery and point people at the KB link.
- Legal: can someone loop in procurement legal for the addendum — I'll need approval to provision the dedicated node (cost center charge).

If everyone agrees, I'll prepare the engineering sign-off ticket and link it here: https://redwood-internal.tracker/EV/1784

Karthik Iyer
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
